138	// walk reads one complete JSON value from the start of the document,
139	// driven by an explicit frame stack rather than Go call frames. Scalars
140	// are consumed in place; an opener pushes a frame (after enforcing the
141	// nesting limit) and its matching closer pops it. The observable verdicts
142	// are exactly the recursive reader's: errUndecided for anything the
143	// encoding/json walk should judge, text errors from string scanning, the
144	// onMember abort, or errJSONDepthExceeded at the 10001st container level.
145	func (w *jsonWalker) walk() error {
146		w.frames = w.frames[:0]
147		w.depth = 0
148		w.nextID = 0
149	
150		// readValue reads one value reached by segment loc from the current
151		// top frame ("" for the document root). A scalar or an empty
152		// container is consumed in place; a non-empty container pushes a
153		// frame and the main loop continues. The walk is over exactly when
154		// no frame remains afterwards (a root scalar or root empty
155		// container); a value read inside a container always leaves its
156		// parent frame on the stack.
157		readValue := func(loc string) error {
158			w.skipSpace()
159			if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
160				return errUndecided
161			}
162			switch c := w.data[w.pos]; {
163			case c == '{' || c == '[':
164				w.pos++ // consume opener
165				w.depth++
166				if w.depth > maxJSONNestingDepth {
167					return errJSONDepthExceeded
168				}
169				closer := byte('}')
170				state := frameExpectKey
171				if c == '[' {
172					closer = ']'
173					state = frameArrayValue
174				}
175				w.skipSpace()
176				if w.pos < len(w.data) && w.data[w.pos] == closer {
177					// An empty container opens and closes the level without
178					// pushing a frame; its parent (if any) moves straight to
179					// the after-value state.
180					w.pos++
181					w.depth--
182					return nil
183				}
184				w.nextID++
185				w.frames = append(w.frames, walkFrame{
186					id: w.nextID, kind: c, loc: loc, state: state,
187				})
188				return nil
189			case c == '"':
190				w.setValueStringPath(loc)
191				_, err := w.jsonString(false)
192				return err
193			case c == 't':
194				return w.literal("true")
195			case c == 'f':
196				return w.literal("false")
197			case c == 'n':

199			case c == '-' || ('0' <= c && c <= '9'):

201				// error at exactly this position: judge the grammar here and stop
202				// on it (deferring the report to the decoder) rather than skip
203				// past it and blame a later string or duplicate.
204				return w.number()
205			default:
206				return errUndecided
207			}
208		}
209	
210		for {
211			if len(w.frames) == 0 {
212				if err := readValue(""); err != nil {
213					return err
214				}
215				if len(w.frames) == 0 {
216					return nil
217				}
218				continue
219			}
220			parent := len(w.frames) - 1
221			top := &w.frames[parent]
222			switch top.state {
223			case frameExpectKey:
224				w.skipSpace()
225				if w.pos >= len(w.data) || w.data[w.pos] != '"' {
226					return errUndecided
227				}
228				owner := parent
229				w.stringPath = func() string { return w.framePath(owner) }
230				key, err := w.jsonString(true)
231				if err != nil {
232					return err
233				}
234				if w.onMember != nil {
235					if err := w.onMember(top.id, key); err != nil {
236						return err
237					}
238				}
239				top.key = key
240				top.state = frameExpectColon
241			case frameExpectColon:
242				w.skipSpace()
243				if w.pos >= len(w.data) || w.data[w.pos] != ':' {
244					return errUndecided
245				}
246				w.pos++
247				top.state = frameExpectValue
248			case frameExpectValue:
249				if err := readValue(memberSegment(top.key)); err != nil {
250					return err
251				}
252				// The after-value state is set even when a non-empty child
253				// container pushed a frame: when that child pops, the parent
254				// resumes here.
255				w.frames[parent].state = frameObjectAfter
256			case frameObjectAfter:
257				w.skipSpace()
258				if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
259					return errUndecided
260				}
261				switch w.data[w.pos] {
262				case ',':
263					w.pos++
264					top.state = frameExpectKey
265				case '}':
266					w.pos++
267					w.depth--
268					w.frames = w.frames[:parent]
269					if len(w.frames) == 0 {
270						return nil
271					}
272				default:
273					return errUndecided
274				}
275			case frameArrayValue:
276				if err := readValue(indexSegment(top.index)); err != nil {
277					return err
278				}
279				w.frames[parent].state = frameArrayAfter
280			case frameArrayAfter:
281				w.skipSpace()
282				if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
283					return errUndecided
284				}
285				switch w.data[w.pos] {
286				case ',':
287					w.pos++
288					top.index++
289					top.state = frameArrayValue
290				case ']':
291					w.pos++
292					w.depth--
293					w.frames = w.frames[:parent]
294					if len(w.frames) == 0 {
295						return nil
296					}
297				default:
298					return errUndecided
299				}
300			}
301		}
302	}

304	// setValueStringPath prepares the lazy location of a string value reached
305	// by loc from the current top frame: the root value is at "$", an object
306	// member value at the owner's path plus its member segment, and an array
307	// element at the owner's path plus its index segment.
308	func (w *jsonWalker) setValueStringPath(loc string) {
309		if len(w.frames) == 0 {
310			w.stringPath = func() string { return "$" }
311			return
312		}
313		owner := len(w.frames) - 1
314		w.stringPath = func() string { return w.framePath(owner) + loc }
315	}
316	
317	// framePath joins the location of the frame at stack index fi from its
318	// segments: "$" followed by every entered container's own loc. It is
319	// called only to fill in an error location, so an accepted deep document
320	// never pays for these strings.
321	func (w *jsonWalker) framePath(fi int) string {
322		var b strings.Builder
323		b.WriteByte('$')
324		for i := 0; i <= fi; i++ {
325			b.WriteString(w.frames[i].loc)
326		}
327		return b.String()
328	}

330	// framePathByID renders the current location of an entered container by
331	// its unique frame id, for a callback that needs to report its owner.
332	func (w *jsonWalker) framePathByID(id uint64) string {
333		for i := range w.frames {
334			if w.frames[i].id == id {
335				return w.framePath(i)
336			}
337		}
338		return "$"
339	}

341	func (w *jsonWalker) literal(word string) error {
342		if len(w.data)-w.pos < len(word) || string(w.data[w.pos:w.pos+len(word)]) != word {
343			return errUndecided
344		}
345		w.pos += len(word)
346		return nil
347	}

349	// number scans one JSON number literal, judging its grammar exactly as the
350	// decoder would: an optional minus, an integer part with no leading zeros,
351	// an optional fraction with at least one digit, and an optional exponent
352	// with at least one digit. A malformed number — a missing exponent digit
353	// (1e, 1E+), a missing fraction (0.), an illegal leading zero (01) — is a
354	// JSON format error, so the scan stops with errUndecided and leaves the
355	// report to the encoding/json walk, at the number's own position in the
356	// document rather than after some later string. Legal numbers beyond
357	// float64 range (1e400, 1e-400, huge integer literals) are well-formed
358	// here; whether one is acceptable for a given field is decided later by
359	// business validation.
360	func (w *jsonWalker) number() error {
361		if w.pos < len(w.data) && w.data[w.pos] == '-' {
362			w.pos++
363		}
364		if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
365			return errUndecided
366		}
367		switch c := w.data[w.pos]; {
368		case c == '0':
369			w.pos++
370			if w.pos < len(w.data) && isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {
371				return errUndecided // illegal leading zero
372			}
373		case '1' <= c && c <= '9':
374			for w.pos < len(w.data) && isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {
375				w.pos++
376			}
377		default:
378			return errUndecided
379		}
380		if w.pos < len(w.data) && w.data[w.pos] == '.' {
381			w.pos++
382			if w.pos >= len(w.data) || !isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {
383				return errUndecided // the fraction needs at least one digit
384			}
385			for w.pos < len(w.data) && isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {
386				w.pos++
387			}
388		}
389		if w.pos < len(w.data) && (w.data[w.pos] == 'e' || w.data[w.pos] == 'E') {
390			w.pos++
391			if w.pos < len(w.data) && (w.data[w.pos] == '+' || w.data[w.pos] == '-') {
392				w.pos++
393			}
394			if w.pos >= len(w.data) || !isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {
395				return errUndecided // the exponent needs at least one digit
396			}
397			for w.pos < len(w.data) && isJSONDigit(w.data[w.pos]) {

399			}
400		}
401		return nil
402	}

404	func isJSONDigit(c byte) bool { return '0' <= c && c <= '9' }

406	// jsonString reads one string literal whose opening quote is at w.pos,
407	// validating every byte and escape, and returns the decoded contents. The
408	// decoded form is needed for member names so that object paths are built —
409	// and duplicates compared — from the same decoded names the business
410	// validation sees. w.stringPath supplies the location lazily, evaluated
411	// only when a text error needs it.
412	func (w *jsonWalker) jsonString(isKey bool) (string, error) {
413		w.pos++ // consume the opening quote
414		rawStart := w.pos
415		var sb strings.Builder
416		decoded := false // whether sb holds the decoded prefix
417		flush := func(upto int) {
418			if !decoded {
419				sb.Write(w.data[rawStart:upto])
420				decoded = true
421			}
422		}
423		for {
424			if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
425				return "", errUndecided // unterminated: the decoder reports it
426			}

429			case c == '"':

465	// escape consumes one escape sequence (the backslash is already consumed)
466	// and writes the decoded character to sb.
467	func (w *jsonWalker) escape(sb *strings.Builder, isKey bool) error {
468		if w.pos >= len(w.data) {
469			return errUndecided
470		}
471		e := w.data[w.pos]
472		w.pos++
473		switch e {
474		case '"', '\\', '/':

476		case 'b':
477			sb.WriteByte('\b')
478		case 'f':
479			sb.WriteByte('\f')
480		case 'n':
481			sb.WriteByte('\n')
482		case 'r':
483			sb.WriteByte('\r')
484		case 't':
485			sb.WriteByte('\t')
486		case 'u':

499	// unicodeEscape reads the four hex digits of a \uXXXX escape (the "\u" is
500	// already consumed) and, for a high surrogate, the low-surrogate escape that
501	// must immediately follow. It returns the decoded rune: the BMP character
502	// itself, or the non-BMP character a surrogate pair stands for.
503	func (w *jsonWalker) unicodeEscape(isKey bool) (rune, error) {
504		r, ok := w.hex4()
505		if !ok {
506			return 0, errUndecided // malformed hex: the decoder reports it
507		}
508		if !utf16.IsSurrogate(r) {
509			return r, nil
510		}
511		unpaired := &unpairedSurrogateError{
512			escape: fmt.Sprintf(`\u%04X`, uint16(r)),
513			path:   w.stringPath(),
514			isKey:  isKey,
515		}
516		if r >= 0xDC00 {
517			// A low surrogate with no preceding high surrogate.
518			return 0, unpaired
519		}
520		// A high surrogate must be immediately followed by a `\uDC00`–`\uDFFF`
521		// escape; anything else — end of string, a plain character, another
522		// escape kind, or a non-low-surrogate \uXXXX — leaves it unpaired.
523		if w.pos+1 < len(w.data) && w.data[w.pos] == '\\' && w.data[w.pos+1] == 'u' {

525			lo, ok := w.hex4()
526			if !ok {
527				return 0, errUndecided // malformed hex: the decoder reports it
528			}
529			if lo >= 0xDC00 && lo <= 0xDFFF {
530				return utf16.DecodeRune(r, lo), nil
531			}
532		}
533		return 0, unpaired
534	}

536	// hex4 reads exactly four hexadecimal digits. It reports false — consuming
537	// nothing — when they are absent or not hex, leaving the format error to the
538	// decoder.
539	func (w *jsonWalker) hex4() (rune, bool) {
540		if w.pos+4 > len(w.data) {
541			return 0, false
542		}
543		var v rune
544		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
545			c := w.data[w.pos+i]
546			var d byte
547			switch {
548			case '0' <= c && c <= '9':
549				d = c - '0'
550			case 'a' <= c && c <= 'f':
551				d = c - 'a' + 10
552			case 'A' <= c && c <= 'F':
553				d = c - 'A' + 10
554			default:
555				return 0, false
556			}
557			v = v*16 + rune(d)
558		}
559		w.pos += 4
560		return v, true
561	}

563	// memberSegment renders how one object member extends its owner's location:
564	// dot notation for a simple identifier name, otherwise brackets around a
565	// JSON-encoded string.
566	func memberSegment(key string) string {
567		if isSimpleMemberName(key) {
568			return "." + key
569		}
570		return "[" + jsonEncodePathString(key) + "]"
571	}

577	}

592		for i, r := range key {
593			switch {
594			case r == '_' || ('a' <= r && r <= 'z') || ('A' <= r && r <= 'Z'):
595			case i > 0 && ('0' <= r && r <= '9'):
596			default:
597				return false
598			}

620			panic(fmt.Sprintf("json.Marshal(%q): %v", key, err))
621		}
622		return string(bs)
623	}

69	// checkStrictText scans the raw document and rejects any string — member
70	// name or value, anywhere in the structure — containing invalid UTF-8 bytes
71	// or an unpaired-surrogate \uXXXX escape. It runs before duplicate-member
72	// detection and business validation, so no rewritten string can be compared
73	// or planned with. A document the walker cannot structurally follow is left
74	// to the later encoding/json walk, which reports the format error. A
75	// malformed number is such a stop: the walk never reads past it, so a
76	// number format error earlier in the document is reported as the JSON
77	// format error it is, never masked by a text problem in a later string —
78	// while a text problem read before the number keeps its own verdict.
79	func checkStrictText(data []byte) error {
80		w := &jsonWalker{data: data}
81		if err := w.walk(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errUndecided) {
82			return err
83		}
84		return nil
85	}

641	// TestParse_DuplicatePathQuotesSpecialMemberNames covers the disambiguation
642	// rule: the reported location points at the object owning the duplicate and
643	// must encode member names so their characters cannot be read as hierarchy
644	// or array indices. Identifier-style names keep dot notation; every other
645	// name is rendered as brackets around a JSON string whose decoding restores
646	// the exact member name. Arrays still use their real zero-based index.
647	func TestParse_DuplicatePathQuotesSpecialMemberNames(t *testing.T) {
648		base := `"app":"a","revision":"r","image":"i","batchSize":1,"clusters":[]`
649		cases := []struct {
650			name      string
651			body      string // JSON body without outer braces
652			wantField string
653			wantPath  string
654		}{
655			{
656				name:      "top-level dotted-name object is bracketed",
657				body:      base + `,"meta.info":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
658				wantField: "x",
659				wantPath:  `$["meta.info"]`,
660			},
661			{
662				name:      "nested meta then info stays dotted",
663				body:      base + `,"meta":{"info":{"x":1,"x":2}}`,
664				wantField: "x",
665				wantPath:  `$.meta.info`,
666			},
667			{
668				name:      "dotted name duplicated inside simple object",
669				body:      base + `,"meta":{"x.y":1,"x.y":2}`,
670				wantField: "x.y",
671				wantPath:  `$.meta`,
672			},
673			{
674				name:      "name looking like array access stays one member",
675				body:      base + `,"zone[0]":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
676				wantField: "x",
677				wantPath:  `$["zone[0]"]`,
678			},
679			{
680				name:      "array-like name nested in another object",
681				body:      base + `,"a":{"zone[0]":{"x":1,"x":2}}`,
682				wantField: "x",
683				wantPath:  `$.a["zone[0]"]`,
684			},
685			{
686				name:      "dotted object name in front of a real array",
687				body:      base + `,"a.b":[{"x":1,"x":2}]`,
688				wantField: "x",
689				wantPath:  `$["a.b"][0]`,
690			},
691			{
692				name:      "two dotted levels",
693				body:      base + `,"a.b":{"c.d":{"x":1,"x":2}}`,
694				wantField: "x",
695				wantPath:  `$["a.b"]["c.d"]`,
696			},
697			{
698				name:      "real array index then bracketed name",
699				body:      base + `,"items":[{"a.b":{"x":1,"x":2}}]`,
700				wantField: "x",
701				wantPath:  `$.items[0]["a.b"]`,
702			},
703			{
704				name:      "empty member name as owning object",
705				body:      base + `,"":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
706				wantField: "x",
707				wantPath:  `$[""]`,
708			},
709			{
710				name:      "quote in member name",
711				body:      base + `,"a\"b":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
712				wantField: "x",
713				wantPath:  `$["a\"b"]`,
714			},
715			{
716				name:      "backslash in member name",
717				body:      base + `,"a\\b":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
718				wantField: "x",
719				wantPath:  `$["a\\b"]`,
720			},
721			{
722				name:      "newline in member name",
723				body:      base + `,"a\nb":{"x":1,"x":2}`,
724				wantField: "x",
725				wantPath:  `$["a\nb"]`,
726			},
727			{
728				name:      "leading digit uses brackets",
729				body:      base + `,"1x":{"y":1,"y":2}`,
730				wantField: "y",
731				wantPath:  `$["1x"]`,
732			},
733			{
734				name:      "underscore start keeps dot",
735				body:      base + `,"_x1":{"y":1,"y":2}`,
736				wantField: "y",
737				wantPath:  `$._x1`,
738			},
739			{
740				name:      "non-ASCII letter uses brackets",
741				body:      base + `,"名":{"y":1,"y":2}`,
742				wantField: "y",
743				wantPath:  `$["名"]`,
744			},
745			{
746				name:      "simple existing paths unchanged through tags",
747				body:      `"app":"a","revision":"r","image":"i","batchSize":1,"clusters":[{"id":"x","tags":{"env":1,"env":2}}]`,
748				wantField: "env",
749				wantPath:  `$.clusters[0].tags`,
750			},
751		}
752		for _, tc := range cases {
753			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
754				err := parseDupErr(t, "{"+tc.body+"}")
755				dme, ok := err.(*duplicateMemberError)
756				if !ok {
757					t.Fatalf("expected *duplicateMemberError, got %T: %v", err, err)
758				}
759				if dme.field != tc.wantField {
760					t.Fatalf("field = %q, want %q", dme.field, tc.wantField)
761				}
762				if dme.path != tc.wantPath {
763					t.Fatalf("path = %q, want %q", dme.path, tc.wantPath)
764				}
765			})
766		}

769	// TestParse_DuplicatePathBracketSegmentsDecodeBack extracts every bracketed
770	// JSON-string segment from a reported location and JSON-decodes it: each
771	// segment must restore the exact decoded member name, including quotes,
772	// backslashes, newlines and the empty string.
773	func TestParse_DuplicatePathBracketSegmentsDecodeBack(t *testing.T) {
774		base := `"app":"a","revision":"r","image":"i","batchSize":1,"clusters":[]`
775		cases := []struct {
776			body     string
777			wantSegs []string
778		}{
779			{base + `,"meta.info":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{"meta.info"}},
780			{base + `,"zone[0]":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{"zone[0]"}},
781			{base + `,"":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{""}},
782			{base + `,"a\"b":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{`a"b`}},
783			{base + `,"a\\b":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{`a\b`}},
784			{base + `,"a\nb":{"x":1,"x":2}`, []string{"a\nb"}},
785			{base + `,"a.b":{"c.d":{"x":1,"x":2}}`, []string{"a.b", "c.d"}},
786		}
787		for i, tc := range cases {
788			err := parseDupErr(t, "{"+tc.body+"}")
789			dme := err.(*duplicateMemberError)
790			rest := dme.path
791			var got []string
792			for {
793				open := strings.Index(rest, "[\"")
794				if open < 0 {
795					break
796				}
797				j := open + 2
798				for j < len(rest) {
799					if rest[j] == '\\' {
800						j += 2
801						continue
802					}
803					if rest[j] == '"' && j+1 < len(rest) && rest[j+1] == ']' {
804						break
805					}
806					j++
807				}
808				var s string
809				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rest[open+1:j+1]), &s); err != nil {
810					t.Fatalf("case %d: segment %q is not legal JSON: %v", i, rest[open+1:j+1], err)
811				}
812				got = append(got, s)
813				rest = rest[j+2:]
814			}
815			if len(got) != len(tc.wantSegs) {
816				t.Fatalf("case %d: decoded segments %q, want %q (path %s)", i, got, tc.wantSegs, dme.path)
817			}
818			for k := range got {
819				if got[k] != tc.wantSegs[k] {
820					t.Fatalf("case %d: segment %d = %q, want %q", i, k, got[k], tc.wantSegs[k])
821				}
822			}
823		}
824	}

完成。问题根因与修复如下：

## 问题

- 位置中的成员名由 `darksafe/jsonwalk.go` 的 `jsonEncodePathString` 渲染，它用 `json.Marshal`，而 `encoding/json` 对 DEL（U+007F）和 C1 控制字符（U+0080–U+009F）原样输出，导致这些控制字符真实进入错误位置文字（U+0085 NEL 等会产生控制效果）。
- 重复成员错误 `duplicateMemberError.Error()` 用 Go 的 `%q` 显示字段名，而 `%q` 把 DEL/C1 写成 JSON 无法解码的 `\xNN`。

## 修改

**`darksafe/jsonwalk.go`** — 将 `jsonEncodePathString` 改为手写的 JSON 字符串编码器：
- DEL（U+007F）、全部 C1（U+0080–U+009F）与 C0 控制字符、U+2028/U+2029 一律输出真实 JSON 转义 `\uXXXX`；
- 保留既有规则：短转义（`"`、`\`、`\n`、`\t` 等）、`<>&` 的 HTML 转义、中文/emoji 等可见字符直出、空名与点号/方括号/引号/反斜杠的方括号包裹；
- 永不输出 `\xNN`；每个引号片段都能按 JSON 解码还原原始成员名；含真实控制字符的名字与普通文字 `\u0085`（`\\u0085`）区分清楚；
- 成员名按解码后的 Go 字符串渲染，所以直接书写与等价 `\uXXXX` 书写产生完全一致的位置；数组仍用真实零基下标。

**`darksafe/plan.go`** — 重复成员错误的字段名改用 `jsonEncodePathString` 渲染，不再用 `%q`。

**`darksafe/control_char_path_test.go`**（新增）— 覆盖：
- `$["meta\u0085info"]` 拥有重复 `x`；问题在 `note` 值中时为 `$["meta\u0085info"].note`；非法文本出现在成员名本身时指向所属对象 `$`；
- DEL、U+0080、U+009F、U+2028/U+2029、换行、嵌套与真实数组下标；
- 每个引号片段 JSON 解码还原、无 `\xNN`、无原始控制字符；
- 字面书写与 `\uXXXX` 书写位置一致；普通文字 `\\u0085` 可区分；
- 含这些字符的合法成员名仍被接受且不影响发布计划；CLI 退出码 1、stdout 为空、stderr 说明原有问题。

错误种类与判定先后、Go 入口的零值配置返回均未改动；已确认新测试在旧实现上失败、修复后通过，全量 `go test`、`go vet`、`gofmt` 均通过。
